chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Writing simple chords for Rainy Night in Georgia
summary: Smith wrote out bar-by-bar chords so Boston could play Rainy Night in Georgia for a club's bosses.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: If you write out chords for Boston, can he follow them?
No, he can't follow them either.
No. I wrote out some chords the other day, and I had him up here one night last week, on this number with Brook Benton, this thing called "A Rainy Night In Georgia" that the
people kept asking for up there...

So I wrote it out, and had the chords there. I said, 'Boston, listen. We got to play this. The man told us don't come back up here unless we have that 'Rainy Night In Georgia.' And both bosses, a colored boy and the White man too. And I said, 'We got to have it.' And I said, 'Now, look here. I'm going to write them chords out simple.' And I just put them down there, and I didn't put no accidental or nothin' like that. I just put it down there, if it says A, if there's a B-flat and all that, and an A-flat and E-flat. I just put them down, and nothin' changed and nothin' pretty in it, and just gave it to him. 'Now, Boston,' I said, 'you see them four marks on that bar? That means hit that chord four times, and you just count it across the bar -- one-two-three-four, one-two-three-four.' And that's the way he followed it, and I played on the guitar. And it wasn't hard nohow, and I played it on my guitar, and he got it right down. That's the way he go about it.
